name: Beast Realm Maneater
loreTies: A predator from a Beast Realm where instinct became law. It is not evil in a human sense; it is a living argument that survival has no court of appeal.
Tracks wounded Deities and escalates if ignored.
shortBackstory: Beast Realm Maneater is a non-playable Beast Realm Creature whose origin makes The First Reopening visible as living battlefield danger.

chapters.title: Origin
chapters.text: Beast Realm Maneater crossed from a Beast Realm where survival itself became government. It is not a faction citizen and should never read like a recruitable Deity. Its existence proves that the Gate crisis produces consequences, predators, remnants, and catastrophes beyond civilized armies.

chapters.title: Lore Function
chapters.text: As a Beast Realm Creature from Beast Realms, Beast carries a specific warning into the story: A predator from a Beast Realm where instinct became law. It is not evil in a human sense; it is a living argument that survival has no court of appeal. This makes the creature useful as canon pressure, not random enemy dressing.

chapters.title: Battlefield Behavior
chapters.text: On the map, Beast supports its lore through behavior: Tracks wounded Deities and escalates if ignored. Its abilities — Pounce, Blood-Scent Mark, Devour Weakness — should feel like the environment and story acting through a threat body.

chapters.title: Campaign Tie
chapters.text: In The First Reopening, Beast connects to the warning that not every threat is evil; some are Realm law sharpened into hunger. Encounter designers can place it where the player needs to feel what the Gate has damaged: memory, structure, instinct, oath, water, stone, or command.

chapters.title: Visual / Reading Rule
chapters.text: The creature page must preserve the distinction between Deities, NPCs, and non-playable threats. Beast can be studied under Creatures and Backstories, but its profile should reinforce danger, not companionship.

developmentStatus: Readable creature profile integrated into dashboard threat pages.
